# openobserve_alert (Resource)

Manages an OpenObserve alert.

An alert evaluates a query against a stream and notifies one or more destinations when the result crosses a threshold. Set `is_real_time` for alerts that fire as matching data arrives; leave it false for scheduled alerts driven by `trigger_condition.frequency`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A scheduled SQL alert: fire when errors exceed 100 in a 15 minute window.
resource "openobserve_alert" "high_error_rate" {
  name        = "high-error-rate"
  stream_type = "logs"
  stream_name = openobserve_stream.app_logs.name
  description = "Error volume is above the normal baseline"

  destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.slack.name]

  query_condition {
    type = "sql"
    sql  = "SELECT count(*) AS total FROM \"app_logs\" WHERE level = 'error'"
  }

  trigger_condition {
    period            = 15
    operator          = ">="
    threshold         = 100
    warning_threshold = 50
    frequency         = 5
    silence           = 60
  }
}

# A real-time alert: fire as soon as a matching record arrives.
resource "openobserve_alert" "payment_failure" {
  name         = "payment-failure"
  stream_type  = "logs"
  stream_name  = "payments"
  is_real_time = true

  destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.pagerduty.name]
  priority     = 1
  tags         = ["prod", "service:payments"]

  query_condition {
    type = "custom"
    conditions = jsonencode({
      or = [
        { column = "status", operator = "=", value = "failed", ignore_case = false },
      ]
    })
  }

  trigger_condition {
    period    = 1
    operator  = ">="
    threshold = 1
    frequency = 1
  }
}

# An aggregation alert on a cron schedule, evaluated per service.
resource "openobserve_alert" "slow_service" {
  name        = "slow-service"
  stream_type = "logs"
  stream_name = openobserve_stream.app_logs.name
  folder_id   = openobserve_folder.platform_alerts.folder_id

  destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.oncall_email.name]

  query_condition {
    type = "custom"

    aggregation {
      group_by      = ["service"]
      function      = "p95"
      multi_alert   = true
      warning_value = 500

      having {
        column   = "duration_ms"
        operator = ">"
        value    = "1000"
      }
    }
  }

  trigger_condition {
    frequency_type = "cron"
    cron           = "*/10 * * * *"
    timezone       = "UTC"
    period         = 10
    operator       = ">="
    threshold      = 1
    silence        = 30
  }
}

# A PromQL alert on a metrics stream.
resource "openobserve_alert" "cpu_saturation" {
  name        = "cpu-saturation"
  stream_type = "metrics"
  stream_name = "node_cpu_seconds_total"

  destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.slack.name]

  query_condition {
    type   = "promql"
    promql = "avg by (instance) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!=\"idle\"}[5m]))"

    promql_condition {
      column   = "value"
      operator = ">"
      value    = "0.9"
    }
  }

  trigger_condition {
    period    = 5
    frequency = 5
    operator  = ">="
    threshold = 1
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Alert name, unique within the folder.
- `stream_name` (String) Stream the alert queries.
- `stream_type` (String) Stream type the alert queries: `logs`, `metrics`, or `traces`.

### Optional

- `context_attributes` (Map of String) Extra key/value pairs made available to the notification template.
- `description` (String) What the alert monitors.
- `destinations` (Set of String) Names of the `openobserve_alert_destination` resources notified when the alert fires.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the alert is evaluated. Disabled alerts stay configured but never fire.
- `folder_id` (String) Alert folder that holds this alert. Use `openobserve_folder` with `folder_type = "alerts"` to create one.
- `is_real_time` (Boolean) Evaluate as data arrives instead of on a schedule.
- `org_id` (String) Organization the alert belongs to. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.
- `owner` (String) Email of the alert owner. Defaults to the account the provider authenticates as.
- `priority` (Number) Triage priority from 1 (most urgent) to 5. Display metadata only; it does not affect when the alert fires.
- `query_condition` (Block, Optional) What the alert evaluates. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--query_condition))
- `row_template` (String) Template applied to each matched row when rendering `{rows}` in the message.
- `tags` (Set of String) Selection tags such as `prod` or `service:checkout`.
- `template` (String) Template used for every destination, overriding each destination's own template. Lets one set of destinations serve alerts with different message formats.
- `trigger_condition` (Block, Optional) When and how often the alert is evaluated, and what counts as firing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--trigger_condition))
- `tz_offset` (Number) Timezone offset in minutes, negative west of UTC.

### Read-Only

- `alert_id` (String) Server-assigned alert identifier.
- `id` (String) Resource ID in the format `{org_id}/{alert_id}`.
- `last_edited_by` (String) Account that last modified the alert.
- `last_satisfied_at` (Number) Timestamp of the last time the alert condition was met, in microseconds.
- `last_triggered_at` (Number) Timestamp of the last time the alert fired, in microseconds.
- `updated_at` (Number) Timestamp of the last modification, in microseconds.

<a id="nestedblock--query_condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `query_condition`

Optional:

- `aggregation` (Block, Optional) Aggregation applied before the threshold comparison. Only used when `type` is `custom`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--query_condition--aggregation))
- `conditions` (String) Filter conditions for `custom` alerts, as a JSON document. Use `jsonencode()` to build it. Both the flat and the nested (grouped) condition formats are accepted.
- `multi_time_range` (Block List) Historical windows to compare the current window against. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--query_condition--multi_time_range))
- `promql` (String) PromQL expression. Required when `type` is `promql`.
- `promql_condition` (Block, Optional) Comparison applied to the PromQL result. Required when `type` is `promql`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--query_condition--promql_condition))
- `search_event_type` (String) Search event classification recorded for the alert's queries.
- `sql` (String) SQL query returning an aggregate to compare against the threshold. Required when `type` is `sql`.
- `type` (String) Query style: `custom` (UI-style conditions, default), `sql`, or `promql`.
- `vrl_function` (String) VRL function applied to results before evaluation.

<a id="nestedblock--query_condition--aggregation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `query_condition.aggregation`

Optional:

- `function` (String) Aggregate function: `avg`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `count`, `median`, or a percentile such as `p95`.
- `group_by` (List of String) Columns to group by before aggregating.
- `having` (Block, Optional) Critical threshold applied to the aggregate value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--query_condition--aggregation--having))
- `multi_alert` (Boolean) Evaluate and notify per group instead of collapsing to a single result. Requires a non-empty `group_by`.
- `warning_value` (Number) Warning-level threshold for the aggregate, sharing the operator and column of `having`. Must be strictly less severe than the critical value.

<a id="nestedblock--query_condition--aggregation--having"></a>
### Nested Schema for `query_condition.aggregation.having`

Optional:

- `column` (String) Column the comparison reads.
- `operator` (String) Comparison operator: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `Contains`, or `NotContains`.
- `value` (String) Value to compare against. A value that parses as a number is sent as a JSON number; anything else is sent as a JSON string.



<a id="nestedblock--query_condition--multi_time_range"></a>
### Nested Schema for `query_condition.multi_time_range`

Required:

- `offset` (String) How far back the comparison window sits, for example `1h` or `1d`.


<a id="nestedblock--query_condition--promql_condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `query_condition.promql_condition`

Optional:

- `column` (String) Column the comparison reads.
- `operator` (String) Comparison operator: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `Contains`, or `NotContains`.
- `value` (String) Value to compare against. A value that parses as a number is sent as a JSON number; anything else is sent as a JSON string.



<a id="nestedblock--trigger_condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trigger_condition`

Optional:

- `align_time` (Boolean) Align each query window to period boundaries.
- `cron` (String) Cron expression. Required when `frequency_type` is `cron`.
- `frequency` (Number) How often the alert runs, in minutes. Used when `frequency_type` is `minutes`.
- `frequency_type` (String) Scheduling style: `minutes` (default) or `cron`.
- `notify_on_warning` (Boolean) Whether a warning-level match sends a notification. Defaults to true; set false to record warnings without paging.
- `operator` (String) Operator comparing the result to `threshold`.
- `period` (Number) Lookback window in minutes that each evaluation queries.
- `silence` (Number) Minutes to stay quiet after firing before the alert may fire again.
- `threshold` (Number) Critical threshold the result is compared against.
- `timezone` (String) Timezone for the cron schedule, for example `America/New_York`.
- `tolerance_in_secs` (Number) Tolerance in seconds applied to the evaluation window boundaries.
- `warning_threshold` (Number) Warning threshold sharing `operator` with the critical one. Must be strictly less severe than `threshold`; omit for a single-level alert.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Alerts are imported as {org_id}/{alert_id}.
# Find the alert ID with the openobserve_alerts data source or the UI URL.
terraform import openobserve_alert.high_error_rate default/2fXkZ8QlmNbYcV1pR3sT
```
